events.title: Disabled hauler recovery
events.arrangement: Hauler drifts off lane-center shedding speed; responders stack around it - tender abeam, tug astern, patrol standing 60 wu off
events.startConditions: Hauler wear/damage roll mid-transit (or combat aftermath with a survivor)
events.visibleCue: A loaded hull decelerating where no destination exists, drive glow dying stutter by stutter

phases.name: failure
phases.visible: Drive dies; hauler coasts off-lane in a slow visible yaw nobody is correcting

phases.name: distress
phases.visible: Whole-hull red/white alternation begins (the existing distress code); passing traffic bulges one extra width around it

phases.name: response
phases.visible: Tender DEPARTs its berth and runs the leg; patrol takes overwatch if lawful; tug trails

phases.name: work
phases.visible: Tender abeam: red corners, weld stitch, white bar - hull_open at a casualty instead of a client

phases.name: resolve
phases.visible: Either the hauler's drive relights and it limps on, or the tug kisses on and walks it home

events.completion: Lane traffic re-centers; the casualty either resumes (repaired) or is walked to the station (towed)

interruptions.trigger: Responders beaten to the site by a pirate tug

interruptions.outcome: Distress continues; second response window opens; scavenger events key on the delay
The hauler becomes an honest wreck with full cargo - the player's to salvage

playerInterference: Help: kill nothing, park between the casualty and trouble
Steal cargo DURING the response delay
Attack the tug mid-tow
Protect the recovery for ambient rep
Salvage everything if it all goes wrong
events.criminalOpportunity: The response delay is a countdown everyone can see - the freshest cargo in space belongs to whoever disrespects it first
events.aftermath: Repaired hauler runs visibly slower for the session; towed hulls park at the station apron as persistent set dressing
events.fallback: Casualty despawns: responders converge, sweep the empty point, disperse - a false alarm that still reads as a system working
events.diagramMermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant H as Hauler
  participant T as Tender
  participant G as Tug
  participant P as Patrol
  H->>H: drive dies, coasts off-lane
  H->>H: distress alternation begins
  Note over H: passing traffic gives one extra width
  T->>H: DEPART + straight response leg
  P->>P: overwatch 60 wu (lawful only)
  G->>H: trails in, holds astern
  T-->>H: hull_open work (red corners, weld stitch)
  alt drive relights
    H->>H: limps on, slower
  else tow
    G->>H: kiss + walk to station
  end
events.notes: The brief's worked example. Every beat maps to an existing system; the only new state is 'disabled' (a speed-zero + distress flag the kernel can already hold via FLEE-style override). PQ-045.causal-chain: LIVE on Ceres as link 4; actors ceres_refinery_hauler + ceres_refinery_tender (optional bind); requires hauler_stressed; stamps ceresCausalDisabled for the failure window; seeds miner_wear+hauler_recovered at work so tender-services can open under the concurrency cap while resolve finishes.

events.title: Two miners clip at a crowded seam
environment: one rich rock with two assigned slots (the crowding IS the cause)
events.arrangement: Both work the same face 20 wu apart; one repositioning hop crosses the other's line
events.startConditions: Two miners share a field slot radius (the rich-seam event's greed phase makes this likely - deliberate chaining)
events.visibleCue: Two cut cones converging on one face - anyone who has watched miners knows the spacing is wrong

phases.name: crowd
phases.visible: Cones drift closer; spall streams begin to cross

phases.name: clip
phases.visible: A repositioning hop grazes the neighbor - visible lurch, both cones die, a spray of hull-fragment pickups

phases.name: back_off
phases.visible: Both hulls drift apart tumbling slightly; one flashes distress briefly; dust hangs where they hit

phases.name: sort_out
phases.visible: The less-damaged one re-approaches the rock; the other limps home early with a wobble in its line

events.completion: One miner works on; one limps home; the seam keeps a debris sparkle - the cheapest possible accident with a full story arc

interruptions.outcome: It goes fully disabled - chains into the recovery event with a miner casualty

playerInterference: Grab the collision fragments
Escort the limper home
Take the vacated slot and mine it
events.criminalOpportunity: A limping loaded miner alone on a home leg is the raider event's ideal prey - the chain is obvious and legible
events.aftermath: Field slot marks single-occupancy for the session (the world learns); fragment pickups persist
events.fallback: Either miner despawns mid-scene: the other resumes; fragments persist
events.notes: No physics collision needed - the clip is choreographed (timed lurch + fragment spawn), which also keeps it deterministic.

events.title: Cargo pod escapes a station clamp
environment: station cargo face with a pod stack
events.arrangement: Pod separates from the stack on a slow tumbling vector toward the lane; tug launches after it
events.startConditions: Station cargo face active (hauler_dock or cargo_tractor profile running); failure roll
events.visibleCue: One pod in the stack starts BLINKING its clamp strobe out of rhythm with the rest - wrongness in a pattern the player has seen right a hundred times

phases.name: shear
phases.visible: Pod separates, tumbling slowly, clamp strobe still blinking wrong

phases.name: drift
phases.visible: Pod crosses toward the lane; near traffic bulges around its projected line - everyone can do the math

phases.name: chase
phases.visible: Tug launches (patrol_launch profile geometry, tug dressing) and runs the pod down

phases.name: recover
phases.visible: Kiss, drift-match, walk back to the stack - ev_tug_repositions_cargo's second half, caused instead of scheduled

events.completion: Pod re-stacked; the stack's strobes all blink in rhythm again - closure you can SEE

interruptions.trigger: Pod crosses the lane before the tug arrives
interruptions.outcome: Near-miss bulge in traffic; pod exits the pocket and becomes a drifting prize
Pod drifts free; re-arms ev_tug_repositions_cargo for the next tug spawn

playerInterference: Catch the pod first (finders keepers, with a witness)
Nudge it INTO the lane for chaos
Return it to the stack yourself - the station notices (ambient rep)
events.criminalOpportunity: A pod off the clamp is legally ambiguous cargo for exactly as long as the chase lasts
events.aftermath: Recovered or not, the stack runs one pod short or whole - visible either way
events.fallback: Tug lost mid-chase: pod keeps drifting; the event degrades into free salvage

events.title: Disabled ship broadcasts distress

participants.note: any small hull works; courier reads most sympathetic

events.arrangement: Casualty adrift with a slow tumble; rescue approaches on the textbook wide arc, floods on early
events.startConditions: Existing distress encounter script fires with a civilian casualty
events.visibleCue: The red/white whole-hull alternation - the one signal every player learns first because everything else in the code defers to it

phases.name: alone
phases.visible: Casualty tumbles and flashes; traffic gives it space but nobody stops - the worst part, and it is authored

phases.name: answer
phases.visible: Rescue arrives floods-first (we-see-you doctrine), red-white STEADY against the casualty's alternation

phases.name: alongside
phases.visible: Rescue matches tumble, takes the casualty into its bay shadow; the alternation SLOWS as power transfers - recovery you can read at 150 wu

phases.name: away
phases.visible: Pair departs for the station together, casualty dark now, rescue's steady bars lit

events.completion: Both reach the station; the pocket's traffic re-centers

interruptions.outcome: Casualty keeps flashing; scavenger and tow-theft events key on the extended window

interruptions.trigger: Player reaches the casualty first and holds station 20 s
interruptions.outcome: Counts as the response; the rescue diverts back - the world credits the player by proximity

playerInterference: Answer the distress yourself
Loot the casualty WHILE it flashes (the region's darkest legible act)
Escort the recovery pair home
events.criminalOpportunity: A flashing hull is a beacon for everyone - the same signal that summons rescue prices the victim for wolves
events.aftermath: Saved couriers re-run their route next window (the same hull, a continuity detail); looted ones become wrecks
events.fallback: Rescue role unavailable: the existing distress script's default resolution runs (timeout despawn) - the event only ADDS the visible response when one exists

events.title: Tanker leak forces a work-site evacuation
events.arrangement: Leaking tanker at the pocket's heart; a visible venting plume; everything else moving AWAY in order of sense
events.startConditions: Loaded tanker takes damage or fails a transfer (composes with ev_tanker_loads_at_harvester interruptions)
events.visibleCue: A continuous white venting jet from a tank seam - the one plume in the game that means RUN, and it points sideways not aft

phases.name: vent
phases.visible: Jet starts; tanker's own crew code goes to distress alternation; it turns AWAY from the workers - doctrine even in failure

phases.name: scatter
phases.visible: Miners stow gear (deploy scalar reversing - visible arms folding) and clear out in different directions; the pocket empties inside a minute

phases.name: stand_off
phases.visible: Tanker drifts alone venting; patrol cones the approach at 150 wu if lawful; the emptiness IS the event

phases.name: resolve
phases.visible: Vent exhausts: either the tanker limps off half-empty, or the seam fails and the existing big secondary fires - wreck, flash, and a debris ring

events.completion: Pocket repopulates over the next windows; either a surviving tanker or a rich, dangerous wreck field

interruptions.trigger: Anything ignites the plume (weapons fire through it)
interruptions.outcome: Immediate secondary - and the shooter is visibly the cause

playerInterference: Fly the plume (damage tick, bravado)
Shoot the tank and own the consequence
Wait out the stand-off and salvage first
events.criminalOpportunity: An evacuated pocket is an unlocked room: every claim, stake and cache in it sits unwatched for two minutes
events.aftermath: Detonation leaves a persistent wreck field (class battlefield) that seeds salvage/scavenge events for the session
events.fallback: Miners despawn instead of scattering: the stand-off still reads (one hull venting alone)

events.title: Debris field drifts across the route

participants.note: mule + scoop dressing until donor promoted

environment: cluster of 8-12 debris pickups with a shared slow drift vector crossing a lane
events.arrangement: Debris enters at the pocket edge and crosses the lane over ~2 minutes; traffic threads or bulges around it
events.startConditions: Wreck-field aftermath upwind, or scheduled environmental spawn
events.visibleCue: Sparkles where nothing should sparkle - a constellation moving as one against the parallax

phases.name: ingress
phases.visible: Debris crosses the pocket edge; the first hauler swerves and the lane's whole file inherits the bend

phases.name: thread
phases.visible: Traffic threads the gaps; near-misses read as small side-steps; optionally a patrol cones the worst of it (composes with ev_lane_spot_closure)

phases.name: sweep
phases.visible: Sweeper arrives and eats the field piece by piece, cage visibly filling - municipal heroism at 12 wu/min

events.completion: Lane straightens as the field thins; the sweeper hauls its full cage to the scrap yard

interruptions.outcome: The field crosses and exits the pocket naturally - the event still reads without the janitor

playerInterference: Collect the debris yourself (it is all pickups)
Tow the biggest piece off-lane and the bend relaxes early
Shoot the debris - fragments thin faster but scatter wider (visible tradeoff)
events.criminalOpportunity: Bent traffic at a known point for two minutes - the pop-up toll's site-selection event
events.aftermath: Swept debris ticks the scrap market; unswept pieces persist at the pocket edge
events.fallback: Sweeper lost: remaining debris keeps drifting; re-arms next window

events.title: Repair tug answers a drive-out call

participants.note: the casualty - deep-field worker far from lanes

environment: far pocket edge, 150+ wu from lanes
events.arrangement: Dead surveyor at the far edge; tender and tug fly out TOGETHER in loose column - the pairing itself says the job is uncertain
events.startConditions: Surveyor job fails its cycle (drive-out roll) beyond the tender's usual client range
events.visibleCue: Two service hulls leaving TOGETHER on one bearing with no client visible - a formation that only means somebody far away is in trouble

phases.name: column_out
phases.visible: Tender leads, tug trails 20 wu; both clean-burn on a dead-straight rescue bearing

phases.name: triage
phases.visible: Tender works the casualty first - hull_open, weld stitch on the drive housing

phases.name: verdict
phases.visible: Either the surveyor's pin relights (fixed - tender's gamble won) or the tug moves in and takes the tow (the pairing existed for this)

phases.name: column_home
phases.visible: All hulls return in column, casualty under tow or under power - the shape of the column tells the ending at any range

events.completion: The far edge is empty again; the story was legible entirely from formation shapes

interruptions.trigger: Ambush on the column (isolated, predictable route)
interruptions.outcome: Tug bolts with the tender covering; casualty left - re-arms as a scavenger/tow-theft target

playerInterference: Shadow the column out (they lead you to the deep-field find the surveyor died near)
Hit the column (three soft targets, far from help)
Fix the surveyor first with your own repair verb if you carry one
events.criminalOpportunity: The column's outbound bearing is a straight line to something worth a surveyor's life - free intel
events.aftermath: Saved surveyors resume the probe line; failed ones leave the line dark and a wreck at its end
events.fallback: Casualty despawns: the column arrives, sweeps once, returns empty - a body never found

events.title: Rescue lifter musters at a multi-casualty scene
environment: fresh battlefield (post-combat pocket with 2+ wrecks and survivors flag)
events.arrangement: Rescue takes scene command at the centroid; tender and patrol orbit assigned quadrants; floods light the field like a work yard
events.startConditions: A combat event ends with multiple wrecks inside one pocket (the big-fight aftermath)
events.visibleCue: Mast floods rising over a dark battlefield - the region's brightest object appearing exactly where its darkest hour just ended

phases.name: arrive
phases.visible: Rescue arrives floods-first, bars steady; parks at the centroid

phases.name: grid_search
phases.visible: Rescue walks a visible expanding square; tender trails it welding what can be welded; patrol holds the perimeter

phases.name: recover
phases.visible: Survivor pods (pickups) tractor into the bay one by one - each one a small visible save

phases.name: stand_down
phases.visible: Floods die one mast at a time; the column leaves; the field is just wrecks now - ready for the salvage economy

events.completion: Survivors recovered; the battlefield transitions from emergency scene to salvage field - a visible change of legal state

interruptions.outcome: Patrol engages; rescue NEVER stops searching - doctrine visible under fire

playerInterference: Recover pods yourself into your hold (the rescue accepts the help - and the region notes it)
Loot wrecks DURING the search under the patrol's nose
Kill the rescue and the region remembers that hardest of all (campaign pressure)
events.criminalOpportunity: The wrecks are off-limits only as long as the floods burn - the stand-down moment starts the gold rush, and everyone watching knows the clock
events.aftermath: Field becomes ordinary salvage; saved-pod count feeds campaign pressure valence
events.fallback: Rescue lost: tender continues a reduced search alone - smaller lights, same shape; the doctrine survives its flagship
